podcast.body: Released in 1994, this album by the Los Angeles band Weezer is described as "kind of second wave emo." The band, particularly singer Rivers Cuomo, was characterized by nerdy and geeky aesthetics and highly confessional lyrics exploring fear, bitterness, and confusion, often accompanied by big, loud guitars with punk rock influences. "Weezer from their blue album, kind of second wave emo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Debut Album
podcast.body: Weezer's debut album, commonly known as the "Blue Album," was a significant success that prompted Rivers Cuomo's ambitious plans for their second record. Its "big debut" established the band and set high expectations for follow-up material. "After the big debut of the Blue Album, Rivers Cuomo wanted the second Weezer record to be a space opera."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nerdy Slacker Power Pop; 15 Million Worldwide; Laid Foundations for Emo
podcast.body: Weezer's self-titled debut (known as the Blue Album) was released on May 10, 1994, and defied easy categorization: somewhat grungy but not, nerdy and slacker-ish in a good way, rooted in power pop but with a punk spirit. It was a major critical and commercial success and laid groundwork for emo in the years that followed. Worldwide sales exceeded 15 million copies — a figure many people do not realize. "A lot of people don't realize that Weezer's Blue Album sold at least 15 million copies worldwide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
